comparison: Both evaluate experimental design claims C73-C80. OpenEval finds the design choices well-justified and empirically validated. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about ecological validity, questioning whether simplified stimuli adequately represent real driving scenarios.

Both address the central theoretical claims about spatial contrast distribution (C6, C37-C38, C62, C64-C68). OpenEval supports these claims but notes the mechanistic explanation about central vs. peripheral contrast is inferential. Peer reviewers accepted these as an 'important and interesting contribution' without challenge.

Both evaluate characterization of prior literature (C1-C2, C8-C10, C61). OpenEval finds these claims accurately characterize prior work with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted these background claims without questioning them.

Both address methodological details (C110-C116). OpenEval finds the experimental setup well-described with appropriate controls, including disabled haptic feedback (C112). Peer reviewers express uncertainty about whether haptic feedback could have provided speed information, questioning the adequacy of experimental controls.

Both evaluate claims about perception-behavior relationships (C69-C72). OpenEval supports these claims based on consistent patterns across experiments with independent participant groups. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted these findings through overall positive evaluation without specific concerns.

Both address Experiment 1 findings (C3, C22-C23). OpenEval finds strong statistical evidence with adequate experimental design. Peer reviewers accepted the core findings but raised concerns about statistical presentation clarity (addressed in R6), though they supported the opposite effects of contrast reduction types.

Both evaluate Experiment 2 claims (C30-C31, C34-C35). OpenEval finds strong statistical evidence and consistency between perceptual and behavioral results. Peer reviewers accepted these findings as part of the 'important contribution' without questioning the results.

OpenEval evaluates statistical evidence for Experiment 1 (C21, C24-C25) and finds it adequate with appropriate ANOVA tests. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about the same statistical claims, explicitly requesting clearer presentation of analyses, specification of error bars, and ANOVA details.

OpenEval evaluates Experiment 2 statistical claims (C29, C32-C33) and finds strong evidence. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about statistical presentation across experiments, requesting clearer specification of which differences were significant and ANOVA details.

OpenEval evaluates Experiment 3 statistical claims (C51, C54) and finds them well-supported. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about statistical presentation, requesting clearer analysis details and specification of significant differences.

OpenEval evaluates Experiment 4 statistical claims (C55, C58-C60) and finds strong evidence consistent with Experiment 3. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about statistical presentation and also question trial duration in Experiment 4.

Both address Experiment 3 anti-fog results (C52-C53). OpenEval finds the experimental manipulation directly tests the spatial distribution hypothesis with adequate statistical support. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted these findings without raising concerns.

Both evaluate Experiment 4 findings (C56-C57). OpenEval finds strong statistical evidence consistent with Experiment 3. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted the anti-fog experimental results through overall positive evaluation.

Both address experimental duration and trial design (C117-C119). OpenEval finds the methodological information detailed and adequate. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about potential confounds from prolonged exposure, questioning contrast adaptation effects and sequence effects over trials.
